prompt:
Ultra-realistic premium wildlife documentary trailer, 30 seconds, focused on the great white shark. High-end natural-history cinematography, underwater tracking, long-lens surface shots, slow-motion breaches, stabilized boat-level footage, deep blue water, bright daylight, realistic caustics, subtle film grain, elegant tension, scientifically grounded behavior, no horror styling.

Main subject: one adult great white shark, massive but realistic proportions, natural scars, powerful tail movement, calm predatory behavior, consistent markings throughout.

Secondary wildlife: seals, seabirds, small schooling fish. No humans in danger.
Cold open ocean near a rocky coastline, kelp edges, deep blue drop-offs, sunlit surface water, offshore island habitat.

0-5s: Quiet opening
Wide aerial over a calm ocean at sunrise. Cut underwater: a huge shadow glides beneath the surface.
English voice-over: “For millions of years… this silhouette has ruled the edge of the ocean.”

5-10s: First reveal
Side tracking shot reveals the full great white moving silently through blue water. Close-up on eye, gill movement, tail rhythm and rows of teeth visible only naturally as the mouth opens slightly.
Voice-over: “Not through speed alone… but through patience.”

10-16s: Hunting behavior
The shark cruises below a distant seal colony, remaining deep and almost invisible. Schooling fish part around its body. Camera follows from behind and below.
Voice-over: “Every movement is calculated.”

16-22s: Power moment
The shark accelerates upward through shafts of sunlight. Cut to dramatic slow motion as it breaches clear of the surface in a huge wall of spray, then falls back into the ocean.
Voice-over: “When the moment comes… power becomes precision.”

22-27s: Majestic scale
Underwater wide shot: the shark passes through a kelp-lined blue corridor, then turns beneath the camera, revealing its enormous scale against tiny fish.
Voice-over: “But behind the legend… is an animal perfectly built for its world.”

27-30s: Final iconic reveal
Surface-level shot at golden daylight. The dorsal fin crosses calm water, then disappears.
Voice-over: “The great white shark… master of the blue.”
Hard cut to black.

Photorealistic shark anatomy, authentic swimming mechanics, realistic buoyancy and water physics, stable markings, premium documentary pacing, natural English narration, scientifically grounded behavior, no gore, no feeding close-up, no injury, no text, no logos.
